title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Past price changes show no consistent effect; noise-adjusted lift is x1.0. A 3.4% increase likely reduces demand slightly, but evidence is weak.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: Gift wrap is seasonal and typically sold in cooler months. No past heatwave data; effect is uncertain but plausible. Evidence is thin.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.1. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is raised 3.4% to $5.72. Past promotions show no consistent lift (noise-adjusted x1.0), and post-promotion weeks show no dip (x1.0). The heatwave (38°C) is a known demand reducer for seasonal items like gift wrap, which is typically purchased in cooler months. No prior heatwave weeks with sales data are available, so evidence is thin. The price increase and heatwave both act as downside drivers. Adjusting multiplicatively with weak evidence, shrink toward 1.0. The baseline already includes seasonal trends and noise.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Heatwave forecast: 38°C all week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 11.0 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
